needs_review: UNBLOCKED. The earlier draft was BLOCKED with zero tools because Connector Spec v1 had no client-credentials auth type: basic client_id:client_secret works only at https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token, while the API surface (https://api.spotify.com/v1/*) accepts only 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>', and oauth2_refresh was unusable because it demands a refreshTokenField the vault entry never collects. The new auth.type oauth2_client_credentials (specSchema.js, declarativeRuntime.js getClientCredentialsToken) resolves exactly that gap: token_url + clientIdField + clientSecretField + client_auth basic, which is the flow the two collected fields already support. base_url now points at the API host, not the token host.

The vault entry (services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js:7014) still collects only client_id and client_secret, and that is sufficient: no new field is required and none was invented. Its credential test continues to exercise the token endpoint, which is the correct check for a client-credentials pair.

APP-TOKEN SCOPE ONLY. All four tools are catalogue reads, which is the whole surface a client-credentials token can reach. Anything user-scoped (saved tracks, playlists of a user, playback, recently played) needs the authorisation-code flow with a user refresh token and stays out of scope for this credential type.

Token-acquisition flow is NOT proven by the shape-proof run. The harness fires a dummy bearer at the API surface, so paths, host, TLS and auth handling are tested and the exchange itself is not; only a real client id/secret pair can prove it.

Probe hints use Spotify's own public documentation IDs (artist 0TnOYISbd1XYRBk9myaseg, album 4aawyAB9vmqN3uQ7FjRGTy, track 11dFghVXANMlKmJXsNCbNl) so an invalid-ID 404 cannot be confused with a wrong path.
